advice.msg: use a finite union of declared string keys, or a Record<string, T> dictionary
advice.do: [migration] Only array indices, string indices and declared keys are readable; a computed key needs a `Record<string, T>` type. An open key (a string, a number) on a plain record of data fields is read as an uninterpreted lookup; on a union, a class instance, a record with a method or a getter, or with a symbol or a key call, narrow the receiver, name the field, or bind the key first. In a literal whose type has declared keys, a computed key of literal type names its field and a union of literals is a case split on the key; a `string` key there needs a `Record<string, T>` type.

advice.msg: push on `files`, which is not a local array
advice.do: [migration] This changes what the caller handed in through an alias or a callback. Change it through the parameter itself, or return a new value: `[...xs, v]`, `{ ...r, f: v }`. An array kept in a Map the function builds itself (`const m = new Map<K, T[]>()`, filled with array literals) takes `m.get(k)?.push(x)` while no other name holds its arrays.

advice.msg: write a record field by name, or use a local Record<string, T> dictionary
advice.do: [migration] Only a local array changes by index. Return a new array otherwise.
